correctness.rationale: On D(f)=1 the phase-gauged chart around z^m/√m has first transverse coordinate t z^(m+1) and stable tail w. Critical exponential integrability and Hölder establish real analyticity of exp(|f|²) functional on a small Dirichlet ball; the full stable Hessian is diagonal −(j−1)/m per |w_j|², uniformly coercive relative to ∑(m+j)|w_j|² for j≥2. Hilbert implicit function theorem gives analytic stable critical w=W(t). Rotation and conjugation equivariance force W2=c_m t² and W3=d_m t³ at leading order, with higher modes contributing only beyond degree six. Exact degree-six zero Fourier coefficient on four-mode chart gives reduced Φ=1−|t|^6/(24m)+O(|t|^8), c_m=(2m+1)/(2√m), d_m=m+5/4+1/(3m). Exact orbit distance d²=2[1−(1+s)^(−1/2)]=(m+1)|t|²+O(|t|⁴) on the stable branch; uniform stable coercivity controls all non-polynomial perturbations and the four-mode family gives matching upper limsup. Independent rational Fourier expansion at m=1,4,9,16 matched zero quadratic/quartic coefficients, −1/(24m) sixth term and off-branch quadratic penalties. Infinite-dimensional coercivity and analytical limit rest on proof, not finite checks.
